name: Grove - Ultrasonic Ranger (single-pin trigger/echo)
description: Ultrasonic distance sensor (2–350 cm, 1 cm resolution, 40 kHz, 15° beam). Trigger and echo share ONE pin (SIG): drive SIG high for at least 10 µs, release it, and the module drives SIG high for the sound's round-trip time; distance = high time × 340 m/s / 2 (µs / 58.8 = cm). Runs on 3.2–5.2 V (v2.0 is 3.3 V compatible); SIG swings to VCC, so power it from 3.3 V on 3.3 V boards. Sold as: Seeed Grove - Ultrasonic Distance Sensor / Ultrasonic Ranger v2.0 (SKU 101020010), 4-pin Grove connector SIG, NC, VCC, GND.
eli5: Chirps a sound too high to hear and listens for the echo. The longer the echo takes to come back, the farther away the thing in front of it is.

pins.name: SIG
pins.description: Trigger AND echo (Grove pin 1, yellow wire): drive high ≥ 10 µs to start, then switch the GPIO to input and time the high pulse (µs / 58.8 = cm). 10 kΩ pull-down on the module; the echo swings to VCC

pins.name: VCC
pins.description: Supply (Grove pin 3, red wire): 3.2–5.2 V, about 8 mA. Use 3.3 V on ESP32/Pico so SIG stays at 3.3 V logic

buildNotes: One wire does both jobs: set SIG as an output, pulse it high for at least 10 µs, then switch it to an input and time how long it stays high.
Distance in cm = high time in µs / 58.8 (Seeed's formula: time × 340 m/s / 2). No echo within about 30 ms means nothing in range.
Power it from 3.3 V on ESP32 / Pico: SIG goes as high as VCC, and 5 V would overdrive a 3.3 V GPIO.
Do not hot-plug it (Seeed warns this can damage the sensor); wire it with the power off.
Leave about 60 ms between readings, and aim it at a flat target of at least 0.5 m² for reliable echoes.

driver.code:
# Seeed Grove - Ultrasonic Ranger (v2.0) MicroPython driver.
# Trigger and echo share ONE pin (SIG). Per the Seeed wiki: drive SIG high for at
# least 10 us; the module sends eight 40 kHz cycles, then drives SIG high for the
# round-trip time of the sound. Distance = high time x 340 m/s / 2, i.e.
# cm = high-time(us) / 58.82. Range 2-350 cm, 1 cm resolution.
# SIG has a 10 kOhm pull-down on the module and swings to VCC (3.2-5.2 V):
# power it from 3.3 V on ESP32 / Pico so SIG never exceeds 3.3 V.
# Leave at least 60 ms between measurements so the previous echo has died away.
from machine import Pin, time_pulse_us
import time

US_PER_CM = 2 / 0.034   # 58.82 us per cm (sound at 340 m/s, out and back)
MIN_CM = 2
MAX_CM = 350


class GroveUltrasonicRanger:
    def __init__(self, pin, timeout_us=30000):
        self.pin = Pin(pin, Pin.IN) if isinstance(pin, int) else pin
        self.timeout_us = timeout_us
        self._last = time.ticks_ms() - 60

    def pulse_us(self):
        """Echo high time in us, or None if no echo arrived within the timeout."""
        wait = 60 - time.ticks_diff(time.ticks_ms(), self._last)
        if wait > 0:
            time.sleep_ms(wait)
        p = self.pin
        p.init(Pin.OUT, value=0)
        time.sleep_us(2)
        p.value(1)
        time.sleep_us(10)          # trigger: at least 10 us high
        p.value(0)
        p.init(Pin.IN)             # release SIG so the module can drive the echo
        t = time_pulse_us(p, 1, self.timeout_us)
        self._last = time.ticks_ms()
        if t < 0:                  # -1: echo never went high, -2: still high at timeout
            return None
        return t

    def distance_cm(self):
        """Distance in cm (float), or None when there is no valid echo / out of range."""
        t = self.pulse_us()
        if t is None:
            return None
        cm = t / US_PER_CM
        if cm < MIN_CM or cm > MAX_CM + 50:
            return None
        return cm

    def distance_mm(self):
        cm = self.distance_cm()
        return None if cm is None else cm * 10

    def distance_inch(self):
        cm = self.distance_cm()
        return None if cm is None else cm / 2.54

example.code:
from machine import Pin
import time
from grove_ultrasonic import GroveUltrasonicRanger

sensor = GroveUltrasonicRanger({SIG})
while True:
    d = sensor.distance_cm()
    if d is None:
        print('out of range')
    else:
        print('D=%dcm' % round(d))
    time.sleep_ms(200)
